name: GitHub audit log, users and scanning alerts
description: GitHub Enterprise Server audit events, GitHub Cloud organization membership and the three GitHub Cloud scanning-alert families (code scanning, secret scanning, Dependabot), as Splunk_TA_github indexes them: who did what, which accounts belong to which organizations, and what the three scanners found. Extended here with github:cloud:audit, GitHub Cloud's organization audit log, observed only from indexed dev-Splunk events and GitHub's own audit-log documentation (no raw vendor sample).
source: Splunk_TA_github props, read from a live instance through the configs REST endpoint; GitHub REST API docs for the record schemas; captured samples and indexed events for what each sourcetype carries. github:cloud:audit adds GitHub's organization audit-log events page and the Rulesets REST API page for the branch-protection and repository-ruleset fields that container's sample events carry.

feed.label: GitHub audit log, users and scanning alerts
feed.description: GitHub Enterprise Server audit log events, GitHub Cloud organization membership snapshots, and the three GitHub Cloud scanning-alert families (code, secret, Dependabot), as Splunk_TA_github indexes them.

api_link.label: API navigation link
api_link.description: A GitHub REST API or web UI URL for navigating to a related resource (self link, sub-resource collection, avatar image, html_url page). Not identifying data on its own.

gh_user_id.label: GitHub account id
gh_user_id.description: GitHub's numeric id for a user or organization account referenced on the record (an actor, an owner, an assignee, whoever dismissed or resolved an alert).

gh_user_login.label: GitHub account login
gh_user_login.description: The GitHub handle (login) of a user or organization account referenced on the record.

gh_user_node_id.label: GitHub account node id
gh_user_node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL node id for the account: an opaque base64-shaped string, distinct from the numeric REST id.

gh_user_gravatar_id.label: Gravatar id
gh_user_gravatar_id.description: The Gravatar hash GitHub associates with the account. Empty string in every sample read here, which is the common case for a GitHub-hosted avatar.

gh_user_site_admin.label: Site admin flag
gh_user_site_admin.description: Whether the account holds GitHub instance-wide site-administrator rights. Distinct from organization admin or owner roles.

gh_user_account_type.label: GitHub account type
gh_user_account_type.description: The kind of GitHub account referenced: User or Organization were the values read here; GitHub's schema also names Bot for other endpoints, not confirmed on this pack's containers.

vendor_label.label: Vendor or product label
vendor_label.description: A constant string a container's TA stanza sets to name GitHub as the vendor, product or app for CIM (the app, vendor, product or vendor_product field). The literal differs by container; see each binding's note.

record_kind_constant.label: Record kind constant
record_kind_constant.description: A constant literal a container's TA stanza sets on every record of that sourcetype, for CIM's type field.

repo_full_name.label: Repository full name
repo_full_name.description: The repository's owner/name identifying string, for example octocat/Hello-World.

repo_id.label: Repository id
repo_id.description: GitHub's numeric id for a repository. Stable across renames and ownership transfers, unlike the full name.

gh_repo_node_id.label: Repository node id
gh_repo_node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL node id for the repository.

gh_repo_name.label: Repository short name
gh_repo_name.description: The repository's short name without its owner, for example Hello-World.

repo_fork_flag.label: Repository fork flag
repo_fork_flag.description: Whether the repository is a fork of another repository.

repository_description.label: Repository description
repository_description.description: The repository's own free-text description, as set in its settings. Unrelated to any alert finding on the repository.

audit_action.label: Audit action
audit_action.description: The dotted GitHub audit action name (for example pull_request.merge). The record type of a GHE audit entry: which data.* fields are present depends on it.

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: When the audited action happened, epoch milliseconds. @timestamp and created_at carry the identical value on every record read here.

source_ip.label: Actor source IP
source_ip.description: The IP address the actor's request came from.

actor_geo_city.label: Actor geo: city
actor_geo_city.description: The city GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_country_code.label: Actor geo: country code
actor_geo_country_code.description: The two-letter country code GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_country_name.label: Actor geo: country name
actor_geo_country_name.description: The country name GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_region.label: Actor geo: region code
actor_geo_region.description: The region or subdivision code GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_region_name.label: Actor geo: region name
actor_geo_region_name.description: The region or subdivision name GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_postal_code.label: Actor geo: postal code
actor_geo_postal_code.description: The postal code GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_lat.label: Actor geo: latitude
actor_geo_lat.description: The latitude GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

actor_geo_lon.label: Actor geo: longitude
actor_geo_lon.description: The longitude GitHub's IP geolocation maps the actor's address to.

enterprise_login.label: Enterprise account login
enterprise_login.description: The enterprise (business) account's slug, present only on enterprise-scoped audit actions.

enterprise_id.label: Enterprise account id
enterprise_id.description: GitHub's numeric id for the enterprise (business) account.

org_id.label: Organization id
org_id.description: GitHub's numeric id for the organization.

controller_action.label: Rails controller action
controller_action.description: The Rails controller action GitHub Enterprise Server served the request with, for example merge or create. Close to, but not always identical to, the trailing segment of the audit action name.

actor_session.label: Actor session ordinal
actor_session.description: A small integer GitHub Enterprise Server includes with the request; its exact meaning (a per-actor sequence counter) is not published.

allowed_flag.label: Allowed flag
allowed_flag.description: Whether the action was permitted, seen on pull_request_review.submit records.

review_body.label: Review body
review_body.description: The text body of a pull request review, when the review carried one. Null on records read here.

category_type.label: Audit category type
category_type.description: GitHub Enterprise Server's own grouping of the audit action, for example Resource Management.

client_fingerprint.label: Client fingerprint
client_fingerprint.description: An opaque per-request client identifier GitHub Enterprise Server records with the request. Its internal structure is not published; treat it as an opaque token, not a parseable value.

data_id.label: Generic data id
data_id.description: A small integer id GitHub Enterprise Server attaches to some data.* payloads (for example a review's own id). Its scope depends on the audit action.

issue_id.label: Issue id
issue_id.description: The numeric id of the issue (a pull request is also an issue in GitHub's data model) the audited action concerns.

request_http_method.label: Request HTTP method
request_http_method.description: The HTTP method of the request that triggered the audit entry.

pull_request_id.label: Pull request id
pull_request_id.description: The numeric id of the pull request the audited action concerns.

referrer_url.label: Referrer URL
referrer_url.description: The page the request that triggered the audit entry was made from.

request_category.label: Request category
request_category.description: GitHub Enterprise Server's own bucket for the kind of HTTP request, for example other.

request_id.label: Request id
request_id.description: A UUID GitHub Enterprise Server assigns to the HTTP request that produced the audit entry.

review_id.label: Review id
review_id.description: The numeric id of a pull request review.

server_id.label: GHE server instance id
server_id.description: A UUID identifying the specific GitHub Enterprise Server application node that handled the request, in a multi-node deployment.

spammy_flag.label: Spammy flag
spammy_flag.description: Whether GitHub's spam detection flagged the content, seen on pull_request_review.submit records.

review_state_code.label: Review state code
review_state_code.description: A GitHub-internal numeric state code on pull_request_review.submit records (40 in the sample read here). Its mapping to a human label is not published.

request_url.label: Request URL
request_url.description: The full URL of the request that triggered the audit entry.

user_agent.label: User agent
user_agent.description: The raw HTTP User-Agent string of the client that triggered the record.

cim_dest.label: Computed CIM destination
cim_dest.description: The TA's computed destination of the audited action: an organization, business or host name depending on the action. Null for the pull_request.* and pull_request_review.* actions read here, whose EVAL has no matching case.

device_cookie.label: Device cookie
device_cookie.description: A device-tracking cookie value GitHub Enterprise Server includes on some audit entries. Null on every record read here.

ghe_host.label: GHE appliance host
ghe_host.description: The GitHub Enterprise Server appliance hostname the event was logged on, when GitHub sets it. Null on every record read here.

event_group.label: Event group
event_group.description: A category the TA's github_action_lookup table assigns to the audit action, via a lookup keyed on the action name. The lookup's own value set was not read in this session.

from_route.label: Originating route
from_route.description: The Rails controller#action string the request was routed to, for example pull_requests#merge.

cim_object_path.label: Computed CIM object path
cim_object_path.description: The TA's computed path to the object the audited action concerns. Null for the pull_request.* and pull_request_review.* actions read here, whose EVAL has no matching case.

operation_type.label: Operation type
operation_type.description: GitHub's own classification of the audited action: create or modify were read here; GitHub's audit log also uses delete, not observed in this pack's samples.

failure_reason.label: Failure reason
failure_reason.description: Why an audited action failed, when it did. Not populated on any record read here.

auth_signature.label: Auth signature
auth_signature.description: The TA sets this only for user.login, user.failed_login and public_key.verify actions, to the action name itself. Null for every other action, including all three read here.

cim_status.label: CIM status
cim_status.description: The TA's github_action_lookup table's outcome for the audit action, via a lookup keyed on the action name.

cim_change_type.label: CIM change type
cim_change_type.description: The TA's github_action_lookup table's CIM Change type for the audit action, via a lookup keyed on the action name.

target_user_id.label: Target user id (raw)
target_user_id.description: A raw user_id key GitHub Enterprise Server includes directly on some audit records, naming the account the action concerns. Distinct from the actor and from the TA's computed user field; on the pull_request.create sample read here it coincidentally equals actor_id, which is not true in general.

org_node_id.label: Organization node id
org_node_id.description: GitHub's GraphQL node id for the organization.

org_role.label: Organization membership role
org_role.description: The member's role in the organization.

membership_state.label: Organization membership state
membership_state.description: The state of the membership record itself, separate from the member's role.

enabled_constant.label: Enabled constant
enabled_constant.description: A constant the TA sets to true on every github:cloud:user record; the sourcetype carries no field that could make it false.

cim_family.label: CIM family constant
cim_family.description: A constant the TA sets to User on every github:cloud:user record, for CIM's family field.

alert_number.label: Alert number
alert_number.description: The alert's number, unique per repository and per alert type. Not unique across repositories or across the three alert types in this pack.

alert_created_at.label: Alert created time
alert_created_at.description: When the alert was first created. On code-scanning and secret-scanning alerts this is not the field Splunk indexes _time from; see alert_updated_at.

alert_updated_at.label: Alert updated time
alert_updated_at.description: When the alert last changed. Splunk's TIME_PREFIX for code-scanning and secret-scanning alerts keys on this field's literal name, so it (not created_at) is _time on those two containers.

alert_state.label: Alert state
alert_state.description: The alert's lifecycle status. The literal set differs by alert type: code-scanning uses open, dismissed, fixed; secret-scanning uses open, resolved; Dependabot uses open, dismissed, fixed, auto_dismissed. most_recent_instance.state on a code-scanning alert uses the same code-scanning set, scoped to one occurrence rather than the whole alert.

alert_dismissed_at.label: Alert dismissed or resolved time
alert_dismissed_at.description: When the alert was dismissed (code-scanning, Dependabot) or resolved (secret-scanning).

alert_dismissed_comment.label: Alert dismissal comment
alert_dismissed_comment.description: The free-text comment left when the alert was dismissed, at most 280 characters.

alert_dismissed_reason.label: Alert dismissal reason
alert_dismissed_reason.description: Why the alert was dismissed. The literal set differs by alert type: code-scanning uses a spaced phrase (false positive); Dependabot uses underscored words (tolerable_risk).

alert_description.label: Alert description
alert_description.description: The human explanation of what the alert flagged: the scanning rule's description (code-scanning) or the security advisory's long description (Dependabot).

alert_summary.label: Alert summary
alert_summary.description: The security advisory's short title, seen only on Dependabot alerts (security_advisory.summary).

cim_dest_type.label: CIM destination type
cim_dest_type.description: A constant the TA sets to Repository on every alert record across the three scanning-alert sourcetypes.

rule_id.label: Scanning rule id
rule_id.description: The code-scanning rule's own id, for example js/zipslip.

rule_severity.label: Scanning rule severity
rule_severity.description: The linter's own severity rating for the rule that fired. A different scale from security_severity_level; the two can disagree for the same alert.

rule_tags.label: Scanning rule tags
rule_tags.description: Free-text classification labels the rule carries, for example security or external/cwe/cwe-022.

security_severity_level.label: Security severity level
security_severity_level.description: A CVSS-derived risk tier: low, medium, high or critical. Used for code-scanning's security_severity_level, and reused here for Dependabot's severity fields, which read the same four-word scale.

scan_tool.label: Scanning tool
scan_tool.description: The code-scanning engine that produced the alert: its name, version and an optional guid.

instance_location.label: Finding location
instance_location.description: Where in the file the most recent instance of a code-scanning finding sits: path, start and end line, start and end column.

instance_context.label: Finding context
instance_context.description: The most recent instance's own context: the git ref, the analysis key and category that produced it, the environment, and the commit SHA it was found on.

instance_message.label: Finding message
instance_message.description: The human-readable text of the most recent instance's finding.

instance_classifications.label: Finding classifications
instance_classifications.description: GitHub's own tags for the kind of code the finding sits in: source, generated, test or library.

secret_type.label: Secret type
secret_type.description: GitHub's internal identifier for the kind of secret detected, for example adafruit_io_key.

secret_type_display_name.label: Secret type display name
secret_type_display_name.description: The human-readable name of the detected secret type.

secret_value.label: Secret value
secret_value.description: The detected secret itself, or a fragment of it, as GitHub's schema documents it. Treat as sensitive: this field can carry live credential material.

secret_resolution.label: Secret alert resolution
secret_resolution.description: Why a secret-scanning alert was closed.

push_protection_bypassed_flag.label: Push protection bypassed flag
push_protection_bypassed_flag.description: Whether push protection was bypassed to let the secret be pushed.

push_protection_bypassed_at.label: Push protection bypass time
push_protection_bypassed_at.description: When push protection was bypassed for this secret.

secret_validity.label: Secret validity
secret_validity.description: Whether GitHub's own validity check found the leaked secret still active.

secret_publicly_leaked_flag.label: Publicly leaked flag
secret_publicly_leaked_flag.description: Whether GitHub found this secret publicly leaked elsewhere, for example in a public gist or another public repository.

secret_multi_repo_flag.label: Multi-repository flag
secret_multi_repo_flag.description: Whether the same secret was also detected in another repository.

secret_base64_flag.label: Base64-encoded flag
secret_base64_flag.description: Whether the detected secret value is base64-encoded.

dependency_manifest_path.label: Dependency manifest path
dependency_manifest_path.description: The path to the manifest file (for example requirements.txt) that declares the vulnerable dependency.

package_ecosystem.label: Package ecosystem
package_ecosystem.description: The packaging ecosystem the dependency belongs to, for example pip.

package_name.label: Package name
package_name.description: The name of the vulnerable package within its ecosystem.

dependency_relationship.label: Dependency relationship
dependency_relationship.description: Whether the dependency is direct or transitive, when GitHub can determine it.

dependency_scope.label: Dependency scope
dependency_scope.description: Whether the dependency is used at runtime or only for development.

advisory_id.label: Advisory id
advisory_id.description: An identifier for the underlying security advisory: a GHSA id, a CVE id, or the TA's coalesce of the two for signature_id.

advisory_identifiers.label: Advisory identifiers
advisory_identifiers.description: The advisory's full list of external identifiers, each with its own type (GHSA, CVE) and value.

cvss_metrics.label: CVSS metrics
cvss_metrics.description: CVSS score and vector string for the advisory, in both the general cvss field and, where GitHub publishes them, the version-specific cvss_severities.cvss_v3 and cvss_v4 fields.

cwe.label: CWE classification
cwe.description: A Common Weakness Enumeration id and name the advisory is classified under. An advisory can carry more than one.

epss_score.label: EPSS score
epss_score.description: The advisory's Exploit Prediction Scoring System percentage and percentile, when GitHub publishes them.

advisory_published_at.label: Advisory published time
advisory_published_at.description: When the underlying security advisory was first published. Distinct from when this alert was created on this repository.

advisory_updated_at.label: Advisory updated time
advisory_updated_at.description: When the underlying security advisory itself last changed. Distinct from alert_updated_at, which is when this alert (on this repository) last changed.

advisory_withdrawn_at.label: Advisory withdrawn time
advisory_withdrawn_at.description: When the underlying security advisory was withdrawn, if it was.

patched_version.label: First patched version
patched_version.description: The earliest version of the package that fixes the vulnerability, when one exists.

vulnerable_version_range.label: Vulnerable version range
vulnerable_version_range.description: The range of package versions the vulnerability affects, in npm-style range syntax.

alert_fixed_at.label: Alert fixed time
alert_fixed_at.description: When the vulnerable dependency was fixed (upgraded past the vulnerable range).

actor_is_bot_flag.label: Actor is a bot
actor_is_bot_flag.description: Whether the actor recorded on the event is a GitHub App or machine account rather than a human user.

branch_protection_policy_flag.label: Branch protection policy flag
branch_protection_policy_flag.description: A boolean branch-protection or ruleset setting this event changed (admin enforcement, protected creation, dismiss-stale-reviews, code-owner review, last-push approval, strict status checks, lock-branch fetch-and-merge, or ignore-approvals-from-contributors, depending on the column).

branch_protection_enforcement_level.label: Branch protection enforcement level
branch_protection_enforcement_level.description: Which accounts a branch-protection or ruleset requirement applies to (required reviews, status checks, signatures, deletions, force-pushes, linear history, merge queue, review-thread resolution, lock-branch, depending on the column). GitHub's audit log names the matching update event for each column (protected_branch.update_*_enforcement_level); no value table is given here, since no sample or page read here states the literal set.

required_review_count.label: Required approving review count
required_review_count.description: The number of approving reviews a branch protection rule requires before a pull request can merge.

branch_ref_name.label: Branch or ref name
branch_ref_name.description: The branch, tag or ref name a branch-protection or ruleset event applies to.

event_object_name.label: Event object name
event_object_name.description: A human-readable name for the object the event acted on (varies by action, for example a ruleset or protected-branch rule name).

event_object_description.label: Event object description
event_object_description.description: A free-text description carried on the event, when the action recorded one.

gh_repo_visibility.label: Repository visibility
gh_repo_visibility.description: The visibility GitHub records for a repository named on the event. No value table is given here: no sample or page read for this pack confirms the literal set.

public_repo_flag.label: Public repository flag
public_repo_flag.description: Whether the repository named on the event is public.

origin_repo_full_name.label: Origin repository full name
origin_repo_full_name.description: The owner/name of a repository the event's own repository was forked or transferred from.

pull_request_url.label: Pull request URL
pull_request_url.description: A direct API or web URL to the pull request the event names.

audit_document_id.label: Audit log document id
audit_document_id.description: GitHub's own internal id for one audit log entry (the _document_id the vendor's audit-log schema names).

ruleset_id.label: Ruleset id
ruleset_id.description: The numeric id of the repository ruleset the event names.

ruleset_name.label: Ruleset name
ruleset_name.description: The human-readable name of the repository ruleset the event names.

ruleset_enforcement_mode.label: Ruleset enforcement mode
ruleset_enforcement_mode.description: Whether the ruleset's rules are enforced, inactive or running in a non-blocking evaluation mode.

ruleset_source_type.label: Ruleset source level
ruleset_source_type.description: The level the ruleset was created at: repository, organization or enterprise.

ruleset_condition_target.label: Ruleset condition target
ruleset_condition_target.description: What kind of ref the ruleset's rules apply to: branch, tag, push or the whole repository.

ruleset_condition_ref_pattern.label: Ruleset condition ref pattern
ruleset_condition_ref_pattern.description: One ref-name pattern a ruleset condition includes, controlling which refs the ruleset's rules apply to.

ruleset_component_id.label: Ruleset component id
ruleset_component_id.description: The id of one item inside a ruleset's conditions or rules array (a condition or a rule, not the ruleset itself).

ruleset_rule_type.label: Ruleset rule type
ruleset_rule_type.description: Which kind of restriction one rule in a ruleset's rules array enforces.

github:enterprise:audit.description: GitHub Enterprise Server's exported audit log, as Splunk_TA_github's audit-log input indexes it: one record per audited action (who, what, from where), with a data.* payload whose shape depends on the action.
github:enterprise:audit.note: Splunk_TA_github props.conf: TIME_PREFIX matches created_at or @timestamp; INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS = json flattens the nested actor_location and data objects to dotted field names.

github:cloud:user.description: A snapshot of one user's membership in one GitHub Cloud organization, as Splunk_TA_github's org-members input polls it. One record per member per poll, not an event stream: the object carries no timestamp field.
github:cloud:user.note: props.conf sets no TIME_PREFIX for this sourcetype: _time is always Splunk's collection time.

github:cloud:code:scanning:alerts.description: GitHub code scanning alerts (CodeQL and other SARIF-producing tools), as Splunk_TA_github's alerts input polls the organization or enterprise list-alerts endpoint. One record per alert, holding its most recent finding instance.
github:cloud:code:scanning:alerts.note: props.conf: TIME_PREFIX matches updated_at. The two records seeded in this dev instance come from GitHub's own stale documentation example, which predates the updated_at field; on those two records _time is Splunk's collection time, not an event time.

github:cloud:dependabot:scanning:alerts.description: GitHub Dependabot alerts, as Splunk_TA_github's alerts input polls the organization or enterprise list-alerts endpoint. One record per alert, holding the vulnerable dependency, the security advisory and the specific vulnerability range.
github:cloud:dependabot:scanning:alerts.note: props.conf: TIME_PREFIX matches a created_at value immediately followed by updated_at, so _time is the updated_at value.

github:cloud:secret:scanning:alerts.description: GitHub secret scanning alerts, as Splunk_TA_github's alerts input polls the organization or enterprise list-alerts endpoint. One record per detected secret. No sample or indexed event exists for this sourcetype in this pack's research: every field here is documented from GitHub's schema, not observed.
github:cloud:secret:scanning:alerts.note: props.conf: TIME_PREFIX matches updated_at, confirming the field exists on live data even though no example was found to carry a value for it.

github:cloud:audit.description: GitHub Cloud's organization/enterprise audit log as Splunk_TA_github indexes it: the same action/actor/org shape as github:enterprise:audit, observed here carrying a large share of branch-protection and repository-ruleset policy-change events (enforcement-level and policy-flag fields for required reviews, status checks, signatures, and rulesets).
github:cloud:audit.note: No raw vendor sample was captured for this container; the field list comes from 11 indexed live-Splunk events plus the fields GitHub's own organization audit-log documentation names.

epoch_ms_twins.text: @timestamp and created_at carry the identical epoch-millisecond value on every enterprise-audit record read here; neither is more authoritative, they are copies of the same clock reading.

id_lookalike.text: Two differently-sourced ids on the same record can coincide by chance on a single sample without being the same key in general. Check what each id is actually scoped to before joining on it.

id_url_alias.text: The TA's id field on the three scanning-alert sourcetypes is a FIELDALIAS of url (the alert's API link), not its number. Use number for the alert's own numeric id.

severity_two_scales.text: Code-scanning alerts carry two different severities: the linter's own rating (none, note, warning, error) and a CVSS-derived security_severity_level (low, medium, high, critical). They answer different questions and can disagree for the same alert.

secret_material.text: GitHub's schema documents this field as carrying the detected secret or a fragment of it. Handle and store it as live credential material, not as ordinary log text.

no_timestamp_field.text: This sourcetype's schema carries no time field anywhere; _time is always Splunk collection time, never an event time.

stale_doc_example_no_updated_at.text: GitHub's own published example for this endpoint predates the updated_at field the TA's TIME_PREFIX requires. A record seeded from that example falls back to Splunk collection time for _time; a record from live GitHub data carries a real updated_at and does not.

no_sample_data.text: No vendor example and no indexed event exist for this sourcetype as researched here. Every field is documented from GitHub's schema page, not confirmed against a real record; several column paths are inferred from the sibling alert sourcetypes' convention rather than read directly.

cloud_audit_unsampled.text: github:cloud:audit was read from 11 indexed dev-Splunk events and the vendor's audit-log field catalog, not from a captured raw sample; enforcement-level and policy-flag fields here carry no confirmed value table, only the field's presence and the audit-log events the vendor page names for it.
